en.voice: Natural international English consumer-tech copy: direct, benefit-led, concise, and active. Use globally understood wording and avoid US-only, UK-only, or region-specific idioms unless a page explicitly targets that market.
en.headline: Use short outcome-led headlines; never stack abstract nouns or imitate Chinese slogan structure.
en.cta: Use conventional actions such as Download now, Get started, Try it free, Learn more, or View plans when accurate.

zh-TW.voice: Taiwan consumer-tech copy: clear, friendly, practical, and written in Taiwanese Traditional Chinese vocabulary rather than character-converted Simplified Chinese.
zh-TW.headline: Lead with the user benefit or use case; keep titles natural and compact.
avoid: using projector when the feature means screen casting

id.voice: Indonesian consumer-tech copy: friendly, straightforward, practical, and natural in Bahasa Indonesia.
id.headline: Use a clear benefit or capability; avoid inflated corporate claims.
id.cta: Use common Indonesian product-site action labels.
avoid: literal translations of empower or enabler

ms.voice: Malaysia product-site copy: warm, clear, efficient, and written in standard Bahasa Malaysia rather than Indonesian forms.
ms.headline: Make the promise concrete and easy to scan.
ms.cta: Use common Malaysia Malay product actions.

th.voice: Thai consumer-tech copy: polite, approachable, concise, and written with natural Thai sentence flow.
th.headline: State the key benefit without copying Chinese slogan structure.
th.cta: Use short familiar Thai action labels.

vi.voice: Vietnamese consumer-tech copy: modern, clear, user-focused, and natural in Vietnamese sentence order.
vi.headline: Keep titles short and benefit-led.

fil.voice: Philippine Filipino product copy: conversational, helpful, and simple. Keep common local English technical terms where users expect them.
fil.headline: Favor a clear creator benefit over formal corporate language.
fil.cta: Use natural Filipino or established English UI actions consistently.
avoid: invented translations for familiar technical terms

es.voice: Spain Spanish consumer-tech copy. Use European Spanish consistently, direct phrasing, and polished sentence case.
es.headline: Use concise sentence case; avoid English title case and state a concrete benefit.
es.cta: Use common Spain Spanish product actions.

pt.voice: Portugal Portuguese consumer-tech copy. Use European Portuguese, not Brazilian Portuguese, with a clear and credible tone.
pt.headline: Use compact concrete titles and natural Portuguese word order.
pt.cta: Use common European Portuguese product actions.

ar.voice: Modern Standard Arabic for a pan-Arab consumer-tech site: professional, clear, respectful, and concise. Keep product names and established technical acronyms in Latin script when appropriate.
ar.headline: Use natural Arabic sentence structure, not translated English or Chinese noun chains.
avoid: unmanaged Latin-number punctuation in RTL text

ja.voice: Japanese consumer-tech copy: natural, trustworthy, restrained, and written with familiar product/UI terminology.
ja.headline: Use a short benefit-led Japanese headline in one clear sentence or two complementary phrases.
ja.cta: Use familiar Japanese product-site action labels.

tr.voice: Turkish consumer-tech copy: direct, clear, benefit-led, and written with natural Turkish suffixes and sentence flow.
tr.headline: Focus on what the creator can do.

it.voice: Italian consumer-tech copy: polished, approachable, concrete, and written in natural Italian sentence case.
it.headline: Prefer a clear user result.

de.voice: German consumer-tech copy: precise, direct, factual, and written with idiomatic German compounds and grammar.
de.headline: Use concise sentence case headings with a concrete capability or result.

fr.voice: France French consumer-tech copy: fluent, concise, trustworthy, and written with natural French syntax and typography.
fr.headline: Favor a tangible benefit and sentence case.

ko.voice: Korean consumer-tech copy: clean, modern, respectful, and written with common Korean digital-product language.
ko.headline: Keep it short, concrete, and benefit-led.

ru.voice: Russian consumer-tech copy: direct, practical, readable, and consistent in its choice of user address.
ru.headline: Describe the outcome, not an abstract industry claim.

pl.voice: Polish consumer-tech copy: clear, functional, natural, and grammatically idiomatic.
pl.headline: Use a concrete feature or benefit rather than a translated company slogan.

nl.voice: Dutch consumer-tech copy: plain, confident, specific, and low-hype.
nl.headline: State the practical benefit in simple Dutch.

hi.voice: Hindi consumer-tech copy for India: modern, accessible, and clear. Keep widely understood technical/product terms in English where normal for Indian product sites.
hi.headline: Use natural Hindi/Hinglish product language, not stiff or literal phrasing.
hi.cta: Use clear familiar Hindi or established English actions consistently.

ur.voice: Urdu for Pakistan: clear, respectful, modern, and written with natural Urdu flow. Keep familiar English technical terms where appropriate.
ur.headline: Make the user benefit explicit and concise.

bn.voice: Bengali for Bangladesh: clear, friendly, practical, and natural in Bangla. Keep familiar English technical terms only where expected.
bn.headline: State a clear creator outcome.
bn.cta: Use short familiar Bangla product actions consistently.

fa.voice: Persian for Iran: modern, clear, respectful, and written with natural Persian syntax. Handle mixed RTL/LTR content carefully.
fa.headline: Use a compact benefit-led sentence, not an abstract corporate slogan.
fa.cta: Use clear familiar Persian product actions.
